purpose: Make one pure function the only code in the system that decides when the publisher next runs, and collapse the four divergent default-value sets into one.
design_intent: The operator cannot answer 'it is 14:00, when does the publisher next attempt a post, and why?' without reading seven files. That is the core architectural defect of this initiative: each phase added a correct local decision point and retired none. The target is one function - nextAttemptAt(now, state) -> { at, reason, inputsUsed } - that every other module either supplies input to or reads output from. inputsUsed is the answer to 'not easy to track': log it on every schedule and the run log states which settings produced the decision.
prerequisite: r1-publisher-gate-ordering-v1 shipped AND observed in production for at least one full day.

model_execution_guidance.note: This is the one item in the remediation plan where a fast model should not lead. The extraction is mechanically easy and the decision table is not - getting the outcome x block-state x controls matrix wrong reintroduces the failure class R1 just fixed. Write the table as tests before writing the function.

work_items.title: Extract a pure nextAttemptAt module
work_items.action: Create lib/scheduler/nextAttempt.ts exporting `nextAttemptAt(input: { now: number; lastOutcome: SchedulerTickOutcome; blocks: { publishBlockedUntil: string | null; maintenanceBlockedUntil: string | null }; controls: AutoPublisherControls; multipliers: { trend: number; sov: number; opportunity: number } }): { at: number; reason: AttemptReason; inputsUsed: string[] }`. AttemptReason = 'cooldown' | 'maintenance' | 'error_backoff' | 'gap_recheck' | 'adaptive' | 'already_running'. The function must be pure and total: no clock reads, no I/O, no closure state, defined for every combination of its inputs. inputsUsed lists the setting names that actually influenced the returned value.

work_items.title: Write the decision table as tests before the implementation
work_items.action: Enumerate outcome type x block state x relevant controls as an explicit table of expected { at, reason }. Must include: the R1 invariants (success schedules the cooldown window, an active block is never shortened), each error-backoff step, gap_recheck, and the adaptive path with each multiplier combination. This table is the specification; the function is its implementation.

work_items.title: Reduce scheduleNext to call, clamp, setTimeout, log
work_items.action: Replace the branch cascade in scheduleNext (L230-290) with a single nextAttemptAt call. Log event schedulerNextScheduled with reason and inputsUsed on every schedule. The adaptive multipliers (trend, SoV, opportunity) become inputs to the function rather than a branch that steady-state operation never reaches - this is how F-06 resolves without discarding the lib/analytics work.
work_items.rationale: computeEffectiveIntervalMinutes is currently only reachable from the 'normal' branch, which a healthy system essentially never hits. Roughly 200 lines of analytics and every quiet-hours / jitter / trend dial on the control panel are inert today.

work_items.title: Collapse four default sets into one
work_items.action: Create one exported DEFAULT_SCHEDULER_CONTROLS under lib/scheduler/. Import it from lib/state/scheduler.ts (currently declares its own at L16), lib/scheduler/run.ts (baseDefaults at L28), lib/scheduler/presets.ts, and routes/api/control.ts (hardcoded fallback literal at L316). Delete the other three. Note the values genuinely conflict today - quietHoursStart 0 vs 3, activeHoursMultiplier 1.0 vs 0.8, trendRecalibrationDays 3 vs 7, and targetPublishIntervalMinutes 120 vs 0 - so reconciling them is a behaviour decision, not a mechanical merge. Record the chosen value and its reason for each conflicting field in the spec's resolution log before editing.

work_items.title: Make presets total and sparse
work_items.action: PRESET_CONFIG currently omits gapRecheckIntervalMinutes and enabled, so switching presets inherits whatever the previous preset left behind. Redefine presets as explicit deltas over the single default, and type them so a preset must declare every field it intends to control. Also remove the inline clamp reimplementation at presets.ts:101 - lib/utils.js already exports clamp and run.ts:8 already imports it.

work_items.title: Prevent default-set duplication from regressing
work_items.action: Add an enforcement that fails when a second literal default set for scheduler controls appears. Either a structure rule or a unit test asserting each consumer's defaults are reference-identical to the single source. Without this, the next feature reintroduces the divergence.

acceptance_criteria: Exactly one DEFAULT_SCHEDULER_CONTROLS literal exists in the repository, enforced by a check that fails on a second.
Every scheduler timer is armed from a nextAttemptAt return value; scheduleNext contains no scheduling arithmetic of its own.
Every schedulerNextScheduled log line carries reason and inputsUsed.
nextAttemptAt is pure - its test file constructs no clock, no store, and no scheduler.
Given a run log line, the operator can name which settings produced that interval without opening source.
resolution_log_required: For each field where the three default sets disagree, record the chosen value and why. This log is part of the deliverable, not a side note - it is the only place the behaviour change is visible to review.
out_of_scope: Moving scheduler control ownership into RuntimeStateStore - that is R3, and doing both at once makes the diff unreviewable.

gate_criteria: npm run lint:structure passes with 0 errors
npm run lint passes with 0 errors
npm run test:unit passes, including the full nextAttempt decision table
The R1 regression guards still pass unchanged
